newsitem.title: USA: Rush sees 2nd half truck market improvement.
newsitem.headline: Rush sees 2nd half truck market improvement.

text.p: Rush Enterprises Inc's chairman and chief executive officer, W. Marvin Rush, said "We believe the truck market will improve over the remainder of the year and more specifically during the second half of the year."

Rush said "The first quarter is typically slow in the truck dealership industry and our results are reflective of a generally sluggish truck market." In addition, he added that "the first quarter of 1997 was particularly affected by the recent enactment of a federal brake law just prior to the year end model changes."

The company's pro forma net income for the first quarter ended March 31, 1997 decreased to $785,000 from the prior year level of $899,000. The company reported pro forma results in 1996 to reflect its 1996 earnings as if they were subject to income tax prior to its conversion to a subchapter C from a subchapter S corporation in June 1996.

Rush Enterprises is a heavy-duty truck dealer which provides for the retail sale of new Peterbilts and used heavy-duty trucks of various makes, aftermarket parts, service and body shop facilities and a wide array of financial services.
